Solution
 The same source produces the same current separately, so R = XL = XC. In series, XL - XC = 0 and the net
 impedance is R. Therefore the current is in phase with the source and has the same amplitude as in the resistor alone:
 i = I0 sinωt (or i = √2 I sinωt if I denotes rms current).
 On increasing frequency: resistor current is unchanged; XL = ωL increases, so inductor current decreases; XC =

 the antiparallel component gives uniform translation along -B, producing a helix with radius mv sin120°/(|q|B) and
 pitch 2πm v cos120°/(qB) in the corresponding signed direction.

 The N-theta graph falls very steeply: many particles scatter through small angles and very few through angles above
 90 degrees. Large-angle scattering requires a rare, nearly head-on close approach to the tiny massive positive
 nucleus. Rutherford's model cannot explain atomic stability (orbiting electrons should radiate and collapse) or

 well for r0<r to about 2-3 fm, and approaches zero at larger r. Since F=-dU/dr, the slope is positive for r>r0 in the
 well, giving F<0 (attraction), while the slope is negative on the inner wall for r<r0, giving F>0 (repulsion). The
 minimum at r0 is stable equilibrium.

 drift .Initially, diffusion current is large and drift current is small. As the diffusion process continues, the electric
 field strength & hence drift current increases .This process continues till d iffusion & drift current becomes equal.

 (a)(i) Antimony is pentavalent; it creates a donor level just below the conduction band. Donor electrons are thermally
 excited easily into the conduction band, so electron concentration and conductivity increase. (ii) Formation of a p-n
 junction involves diffusion of majority carriers across the junction followed by recombination, and drift under the
 resulting built-in electric field. Their balance establishes the depletion layer and barrier potential. (iii) Forward bias
 lowers the barrier and narrows the depletion layer; reverse bias raises the barrier and widens it.
